tex_content.html:
Lemma
[radial geodesics have unit chart speed]

↗ lem:dc-ch3-3-5-ball ↗ lem:dc-ch3-3-5-rayode ↗ def:dc-ch3-expmap

1. ch3:3.6There is $ ho >0$ such that for every $v$ with $\| v\| < ho $ and every $t\in [0,1]$, read in the chart at $p$, \[ ig\langle (d\exp _p)_{tv}(v),\, (d\exp _p)_{tv}(v) ig angle _{\exp _p(tv)} =\langle v,v angle _p. \] The radial geodesic $\gamma (t)=\exp _p(tv)$, $0\le t\le 1$, therefore has constant speed $|v|_p$ and length $\ell (\gamma )=\int _0^1|v|_p\, dt=|v|_p$ (the normalized identity $|\partial f/\partial r|=1$).
Proof

\sketch

For $t e 0$ apply the Gauss identity (section 2) at the pair $(tv,v)$:

\[ ig\langle (d\exp _p)_{tv}(tv),\, (d\exp _p)_{tv}(v) ig angle _{\exp _p(tv)} =\langle tv,v angle _p. \]

Pulling the scalar $t$ out of both sides — by linearity of $(d\exp _p)_{tv}$ on the left, by bilinearity of the metric on the right — and cancelling $t e 0$ gives the claim. At $t=0$ the ray package (section 2) supplies $(d\exp _p)_0=\mathrm{id}$ and $\exp _p(0)=p$, so the left-hand side is $\langle v,v angle _p$ directly.

□
